hypothesis: A guarded, standards-backed outer-pipe-diameter-to-DN retrieval alternate will improve candidate recall for valve tenders that specify an unambiguous pipe OD rather than DN, while preserving original-query reranking and selection.
why_now: Current canonicalization explicitly does not interpret pipe OD. This is the documented remaining parser-miss class, and technical evidence supports the exact initial OD 108 mm to DN 100 mapping.
expected_effect: Add at most one DN-enriched retrieval query only for explicit, contextual, allowlisted pipe OD; preserve source retrieval, reranker input, RRF, and final selection.
expected_metric_gain: +0–3.3 pp public and blind hard-pass coverage, with no intended safety regression.
lesson_from_history: Selection-adjacent experiments regressed or were neutral, while additive canonicalization was accepted in cycles 3–4. Cycle 10 was blocked by a protected-file violation before evaluation, so it does not disprove schema expansion. Index enrichment regressed, so this avoids rebuilding.
plan_summary: Created and strict-validated proposal, behavior spec, design, and implementation-only tasks in openspec/changes/cycle-11-pipe-od-retrieval-normalization/. Tasks explicitly exclude GOLD/harness artifacts and supervisor evaluation.
research_summary: The GOST source lists 108 mm as a standard outside diameter; the pipe source identifies DN 108×3.5 as DN 100. The plan limits conversion to explicit OD context and this single documented mapping.
